name.en: Fake Student Finance message: “there’s a problem with your payment”

how.en: Around the times maintenance loans are paid, students get texts, emails and calls that look like they come from the Student Loans Company. They say there is a problem with a payment that needs urgent action, and ask you to follow a link and confirm personal or bank details. Bulk messages often start “Dear Student”. The Student Loans Company never asks you to confirm personal or bank details by text or email.

text.en: A message says it is from Student Finance, often starting “Dear Student”.
It says there is a problem with your payment and your account will be closed if you don’t act.
It gives a link to sign in or confirm your details.
The page asks for your bank details or login.
Dear Student, your maintenance loan payment has been suspended due to incorrect information. Failure to respond in 24 hours will result in your account being closed. Verify your details: [link]

en: A 24-hour deadline or threat to close your account.
A link asking for your bank or login details.
Don’t click the link. Sign in to your student finance account directly to check.
Forward scam emails to the NCSC and texts to 7726.
If you gave bank details, call your bank straight away (you can dial 159).

sources.title: Students urged to stay alert for scams as January student finance payments approaches
